title: Ingress Observability & Quota Onboarding - Mistral Systems

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-27 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Attendees: Samantha Ortiz (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Anita Rao (CTO - Mistral), Marcus Li (Eng Lead), Ruth Delgado (Security)

Summary: Quick intros, then deep-dive into how Mistral plans to route requests (edge gateway/proxy), their quota model, and what telemetry hooks they need. Discussed SDKs (Node/Python), LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters, and requirements that may force Private/VPC deployment. Ended with clear POc and docs to share.

[00:00] Samantha Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros from our side. I'm Samantha, I'm the AE covering Mistral.
[00:07] Daniel Kim: Hi all, Daniel, I'm an SE on Redwood, I'll handle the technical bits today.
[00:13] Anita Rao: Anita here, CTO at Mistral. Leading the platform effort.
[00:18] Marcus Li: Marcus, engineering lead on the AI infra team.
[00:22] Ruth Delgado: Ruth, security and compliance. I'll be asking the hard questions.

[00:30] Samantha: Cool. High level, you sent us a short note — wanting to understand ingress patterns, quotas, and observability as you evaluate hosted vs dedicated vs private. Is that right?
[00:37] Anita: Yep. We're doing a vendor short list for inference providers. Main constraints: PII in prompts, tight latency SLOs for our chat product — sub 150ms p95 ideally, and predictable unit cost for budget forecasting.
[00:52] Daniel: Got it. A couple clarifying Qs: when you say ingress, are you thinking a sidecar in front of Redwood or our gateway as the egress? How do you expect requests routed from your app?
[01:03] Marcus: Right now we have an API gateway on GCP with an edge proxy terminating TLS. We want Redwood to be behind our gateway. Ideally we don't want to open a wide public endpoint for models with PII.
[01:17] Ruth: Also we need audit trails for all prompts/responses, encryption at rest with customer-managed keys, and SSO (SAML) integration for admin controls.

[01:28] Daniel: That aligns with what our Private deployment supports — VPC peering or private link and local control plane options. Hosted can work if you anonymize or use tokenization, but private is common for PII regulated data.
[01:42] Anita: Cost questions: what's the delta between hosted and dedicated for steady throughput? We expect ~30 qps with spikes to 250 qps for short windows.
[01:52] Samantha: We'll share a pricing band but ballpark: hosted is usage-based; dedicated has a base reserved cost but yields lower per-token prices and predictable latency. Daniel, maybe you can give a quick note on autoscale.
[02:02] Daniel: Sure — dedicated pools let you specify min/max GPU capacity and burst. If you expect 250 qps spikes you can set burst capacity or use autoscale policies with warm pools to keep latency low. For hosted, we have routing policies and fallback models to handle bursts, but latency can vary more.

[02:20] Marcus: Important for us: we have existing rate quota logic in our gateway for clients and per-tenant limits. We'd like Redwood to be able to accept a quota header or token and honor downstream per-tenant throttles so we can keep a single source of truth for quota.
[02:33] Daniel: We support passing custom headers and token metadata. You can integrate Redwood's request headers into your quota enforcement. Alternatively, with our Dedicated/Private runtimes you can push quota metadata to the serving layer and apply token-level caps.
[02:46] Ruth: For observability we need: per-route latency, per-model token breakdown, error rates, and a streaming trace for request->response to correlate with our APM. Does Redwood publish hooks or a Prometheus endpoint?
[02:58] Samantha: Redwood Console exposes dashboards, and you can pull telemetry via our API. Daniel?
[03:03] Daniel: We emit metrics to Prometheus in Private and Dedicated, and we have push hooks (webhooks) and OTLP for traces. For hosted customers we provide a tenant-level telemetry feed and per-token cost breakdowns in the console and via the usage API. We also support custom trace ids in requests so you can stitch traces end-to-end.
[03:19] Marcus: Ok, so we'd still be able to link our trace IDs from the gateway to the Redwood runtime?
[03:23] Daniel: Yes, you can pass an X-Trace-ID or our recommended header, and it'll show in logs and tracing. Note sometimes the header is transcribed as X-Tracey ... but it's just X-Trace-ID.

[03:33] Anita: SDKs — we use LangChain in Node and Python, and some teams use LlamaIndex. Do you have prebuilt adapters or do we need to write middleware?
[03:42] Daniel: We have first-class SDKs for Node and Python with LangChain connectors. For LlamaIndex there's a community adapter; our SEs maintain example repos. We'll give you a sample LangChain + Redwood SDK repo that shows streaming responses and function calling.
[03:54] Marcus: Streaming is critical — we need token-by-token to render UI. How do you handle prefix caching and KV cache bumps? We saw references to KV cache optimization in your docs but not the mechanics.
[04:06] Daniel: Our runtime supports KV cache reuse and prefix caching. For streaming, we maintain the KV cache on the server and return incremental tokens; the SDK exposes a streaming callback. There are some caveats with reuse and memory retention — we can tune per-model cache TTLs.
[04:20] Ruth: Security: KMS integration — can Redwood use our customer-managed keys for model logs and stored artifacts?
[04:27] Samantha: For Private and Dedicated we support KMS integrations; hosted offers optional envelope encryption and tokenization. We'll include the KMS integration note in the security pack.
[04:36] Anita: About model fallbacks — if you route to a cheaper model on overload, how do we ensure quality and not break user experience? We want A/B or canary with automatic rollback.
[04:45] Daniel: Our rollouts let you define policies: canary percentage, fallback model families, and quality thresholds (we can tie to a small eval set and revert if hallucination or latency errors exceed thresholds). We surfaced those controls in Redwood Console. There can be some transcription in docs where 'rollouts' read as 'row outs' but it's the same feature.

[05:01] Marcus: Throttling again — can we set per-tenant QPS, per-api-key token caps, and hard daily spend limits?
[05:09] Daniel: Yes: per-api-key rate limits, per-tenant quotas in Dedicated/Private, and spend caps via billing alerts. For hosted we can set tenant-level soft caps and notify, but hard enforcement is more straightforward on Dedicated.
[05:21] Ruth: Audit logs — we need immutable logs for all admin actions, and message-level redaction capability where we can hide PII before logs are persisted.
[05:31] Samantha: We support audit logs with RBAC. For PII redaction, you can use our pre-processing tokenization in your gateway or we can add redact hooks in Private deployments.

[05:42] Anita: Can you talk about expected latency numbers? You mentioned sub-150ms p95. What have you seen in benchmarked workloads?
[05:49] Daniel: Benchmarks vary by model and seq length. For short prompts under 64 tokens on dedicated GPUs we've seen p95 around 80–120ms. Hosted p95 can be higher depending on tenant mixing and cold starts. We'll run a PoC test with your payloads to generate a proper SLO projection.

[06:05] Marcus: For the PoC, we'd like: 1) hosted sandbox perf test, 2) a small dedicated cluster run if hosted doesn't meet latency, and 3) an integration sample with LangChain streaming. Is that doable?
[06:16] Daniel: That's the standard path. We'll spin up a hosted sandbox for you immediately, run benchmarks with your traffic shape, and if needed size a dedicated pool. For Private we usually do a later stage once the contract and compliance boxes are checked.

[06:28] Ruth: Timeline — we need a security review completed by mid-December to keep procurement on our year-end cycle. Can you provide docs and a point of contact?
[06:35] Samantha: Yes — I'll send the security pack and connect you with our compliance engineer. Daniel will run the PoC.

[06:41] Anita: A couple smaller questions — 1) can Redwood enforce request size limits server-side? 2) do you support model pinning per-tenant?
[06:49] Daniel: 1) Yes, you can set max tokens per-request and reject on the serving layer. 2) Model pinning per-route/tenant is supported in Dedicated and Private; hosted supports model preferences but with less isolation guarantees.

[07:01] (short cross-talk)
[07:05] Marcus: Example artifacts — if you can provide a sample LangChain notebook, and a schematic of the recommended gateway pattern (sidecar vs remote), that'll be great.
[07:14] Samantha: We'll attach the sample repo and a deployment diagram.

Recap and commitments
[07:20] Samantha: Recap — Redwood to share: security pack (SOC2/ISO, KMS notes), pricing bands and dedicated sizing guidance, and a LangChain + Redwood SDK sample repo. SE (Daniel) will run hosted sandbox benchmarks using Mistral's traffic sample. Customer to provide traffic histogram and prompt examples.

[07:40] Anita: Sounds good. One last ask: when you share telemetry hooks, we need examples of OTLP traces and Prometheus metric names so our ops can map them.
[07:49] Daniel: We'll include a mapping doc — sample metric names, trace fields, and an example Grafana dashboard.

Close
[07:58] Samantha: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the bench-run and security handoff.
[08:04] Marcus: Thanks, talk soon.
[08:06] Ruth: Bye.

Notes on transcription: there are minor ASR glitches (e.g., 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed 'K V cash', 'SAML' occasionally as 'sample'), filler words intact, and a few speaker attributions approximate.

References & Links Mentioned: 1) Redwood SDK sample repo (link to be shared) 2) Security pack (SOC2/ISO, KMS integration) 3) PoC benchmark plan (spreadsheet link)
